title: Deep Dive: D3.js and Data Visualization
text: Built a real-time SVG map renderer using D3.js and Angular that consumes WebSocket-driven coordinate updates for live equipment tracking. Designed an AnimationQueue as a promise-based FIFO to serialize concurrent D3 SVG transitions triggered by WebSocket events, with adaptive duration control and overflow handling for smooth animation under bursty updates. Used a dual-map pattern (_lastCoords/_targetCoords) to interpolate positions and an interpolateAngle helper with _lastAngle persistence for direction-locked rotation driven by equipment.direction. Implemented fitContentToView and zoomSvgToPointWithRotation with CTM (current transformation matrix) coordinate-space reconciliation to keep D3 zoom and manual rotation from conflicting, resolved via a _customGroupTransform state pattern. Built getNearestCenterLinePoint with lane-direction support for path-aware positioning. Built a PlaybackService tick engine using self-scheduling setTimeout chains for precise timeline synchronization, so recorded equipment movement can be replayed frame-accurately. Debugged and fixed D3 SVG rendering under Angular's OnPush change detection using afterNextRender() and NgZone.runOutsideAngular() to keep animation loops outside Angular's change detection for performance, and resolved memory leaks tied to D3 event listeners and FocusMonitor using Chrome DevTools heap snapshots.

title: Memory Leak Fixes and Performance Debugging
text: Has repeatedly diagnosed and fixed production memory leaks in Angular applications during extended sessions, using Chrome DevTools heap snapshots as the primary diagnostic tool. Root causes fixed include: ChangeDetectorRef references not being cleaned up, FocusMonitor and mat-menu leaks in Angular Material components, D3.js event listeners left attached after component teardown, and an Angular framework-level leak tracked against Angular issue #65922. Applied NgZone.runOutsideAngular() to move hot render loops (D3 animation, WebSocket-driven updates) outside Angular's change detection cycle, both as a performance optimization and to reduce leak surface area. This work significantly improved application stability during long-running real-time sessions on the AtYardNSFT platform.
